drivingQuestion: Is R' Yehuda's measure for crushed earthenware larger than the Rabbis'?
outcomeNote: R' Yehuda's measure is reread as the smaller plastering amount

segments.he: חַרְסִית כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת פִּי כוּר כּוּ׳. לְמֵימְרָא דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְפִישׁ? הָא קַיְימָא לַן דְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבָּנַן נְפִישׁ, דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לִיטּוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ מִדַּת מִנְעָל לְקָטָן. אֵימָא: כְּדֵי לָסוּד פִּיטְפּוּט כִּירָה קְטַנָּה.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: The measure that determines liability for carrying out «crushed earthenware» is «equivalent» to that which is used to knead and make an opening for the bellows to be placed in a gold refiners’ crucible. Rabbi Yehuda says: An amount equivalent to that which is used to make a small tripod for the crucible. The Gemara wonders: «Is that to say that the measure» of Rabbi Yehuda «is greater? Don’t we maintain that the measure of the Rabbis is greater, as we learned» in a mishna that «Rabbi Yehuda says» with regard to reeds: The measure for liability is «equivalent» to that which is used «to take the measure of a shoe for a child?» That is smaller than the measure determined by the Rabbis. The Gemara answers: Here too, «say» it does not mean sufficient material to make the entire tripod, but to «plaster the» cracks in the «small tripod of a small stove,» which requires a minimal amount of plaster.
